definition: Maudlin means weakly and self-indulgently sentimental.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word maudlin. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know maudlin should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By midnight the campfire talk had turned maudlin, with seniors tearfully vowing to text one another every day forever.
Sentimental is much milder than maudlin — a fondness for old photographs, enjoyed with dry eyes.
Teary is weaker than maudlin — tears alone can be sincere and brief, while maudlin means the weeping has turned gushing and self-indulgent.

Weepy means prone to tears — the eyes fill at reunions, weddings, and hospital ads, but the crying itself is honest. Maudlin goes a step past weepy: the tears turn gushing and self-indulgent, performed for their own sake, and the word watches them with a raised eyebrow.

Gushing means feelings poured out effusively — lavish praise, extravagant thanks, delight spilling in every direction, with or without tears. Maudlin is gushing's tearful, self-pitying cousin: the emotion turns soggy and indulgent, and where gushing can stay cheerful, maudlin always droops toward tears.
